questions.question: Does assembled observable evidence satisfy AC-VM-4: For both profiles and both code/refresh/bearer cross-profile directions, wrong-resource use is rejected; same-profile grants work across reload and refresh rotation preserves binding.

Does assembled observable evidence satisfy AC-VM-5: Generate both Host profiles, slash/no-slash MCP paths, unexpected Origins and forwarded/unconfigured authorities: browser mutations require canonical Origin and CSRF; VM Host cannot run browser routes; MCP cross-origin requests are rejected.

Does assembled observable evidence satisfy AC-VM-6: Assembled fixture flows for both profiles complete registration, browser Google owner login, explicit approval, PKCE exchange, MCP initialization and read-only task tool, then refresh and revocation.
Are invalid requests bounded and rejected without exposing credentials?
Are profile validation, transaction binding and HTTP selection owned once through typed seams?
Do behavioral matrices discriminate wrong-profile use and canonical browser composition?
Are Host/Origin/CSRF/PKCE/owner/approval and resource checks preserved for both profiles?
Are local HTTP and live-client limitations documented without claiming deployment success?
Does cross-profile revocation leave both access and refresh grants usable for the issuing resource, in both directions?
Do cookie forms reject missing/null/foreign Origins, while public OAuth authorization POST retains absent-Origin support and rejects supplied foreign Origins?
